elf_linux.target: ELF binary (Linux / embedded; C, C++, Go, Rust)
fast_triage_steps: 1. Identify (<1s): re.re_triage_binary({ path }) -> arch, stripped?, NX/PIE/canary/RELRO, language/compiler, SHA-256.
2. Capability inventory: re.re_imports_exports({ path, filter: 'socket|crypt|exec|ssl|open', kind: 'imports' }).
3. Interesting strings: re.re_extract_strings({ path, regex: 'https?://|/etc/|token|version', limit: 50 }).
4. Candidate functions: re.re_list_functions({ path, filter: 'main|init|handle|parse|auth|verify', limit: 30 }).
5. Selective decompilation of the 2-4 functions that matter: re.re_disassemble_function({ path, target: 'main', mode: 'decompile' }).
1. re.re_triage_binary({ path }) -> native (MSVC/MinGW) vs managed (.NET), arch, sections.
2. Packing check: high-entropy sections or tiny import table -> re.re_firmware_scan({ path }) also reports UPX.
3. Import table by capability: re.re_imports_exports({ path, filter: 'CreateProcess|VirtualAlloc|Reg|Crypt|Internet' }).
4. Managed code: look up a .NET decompiler in the catalog (re.re_catalog_search({ query: 'dotnet' })); native code: list_functions + disassemble_function.

android_apk.target: Android APK / AAR / DEX (Java, Kotlin/R8, Flutter, React Native, Unity)
fast_triage_steps: 1. Fingerprint the framework: re.re_apk_inspect({ path, mode: 'triage' }) -> Flutter / React Native / Hermes / IL2CPP / Kotlin, DEX list, native libs.
2. Harvest endpoints cheaply: re.re_apk_inspect({ path, mode: 'apis' }) -> URLs and REST-looking routes found in DEX strings.
3. Native libraries: extract lib/*.so and run re.re_triage_binary + re.re_imports_exports({ filter: 'Java_|JNI' }).
4. For deep work decompile with jadx / apktool (see the android-reverse-engineering skill in skills-repos).
1. Locate resources/app.asar and list it without extracting everything (npx @electron/asar list).
2. Trace IPC channels (ipcMain.handle, ipcRenderer.invoke, contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld) with grep over the extracted main/preload bundles.
3. Native addons (*.node) can be triaged like any shared object with re.re_triage_binary.

firmware_iot.target: Firmware image / bootloader / embedded filesystem (SquashFS, CramFS, JFFS2, U-Boot)
fast_triage_steps: 1. re.re_firmware_scan({ path }) -> embedded signatures and filesystems (binwalk) + UPX check.
2. Extract the filesystem with your preferred tool, then triage inner binaries with re.re_triage_binary.
3. Hunt configuration, certificates and services with re.re_extract_strings({ preset: 'secrets' | 'urls' }).

go_rust_packed.target: Go / Rust / PyInstaller / UPX-packed or stripped binaries
fast_triage_steps: 1. UPX: re.re_firmware_scan({ path }).upx_packed; unpack a COPY with `upx -d` before analysis.
2. Go: triage reports the language; list the program's own functions with re.re_list_functions({ filter: '^main\\.' }).
3. Stripped C/C++/Rust: work bottom-up - re.re_list_functions({ only_leaf: true, min_size: 32 }) then disassemble leaves first.
